clusters.headline: Venezuela's opposition leader María Corina Machado returns after months in exile
clusters.summary: Machado announced her arrival on social media, writing "I am here. With you."

clusters.headline: Nurse killed in attack while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
clusters.summary: Local youths reportedly accused the health workers of contaminating water sources and spreading Ebola.

clusters.headline: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
clusters.summary: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

clusters.headline: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
clusters.summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

clusters.headline: Africa: African Development Bank Group Advances Sustainable Financing for Transboundary Waters At Iwc11 in Bali
clusters.summary: [African Development Bank (AfDB)] WHAT: African Development Bank Group participation at the 11th Global Environment Facility (GEF) Biennial International Waters Conference (IWC11)   WHO: African Development Bank Group   WHEN: 17-22 October 2026   WHERE: Anvaya Beach Resort, Bali, Indonesia

clusters.headline: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
clusters.summary: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

clusters.headline: Uganda says it has no active Ebola cases, but infections in Kenya and Nigeria are prompting fresh scrutiny
clusters.summary: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection.

clusters.headline: Why Russia's arrest of Japanese journalist is the latest sign of deteriorating ties between the countries.
clusters.summary: Japan is demanding access to a journalist who was arrested by Russian security services. The Kremlin claims that Japan is using journalists as spies.

clusters.headline: Venezuela: Opposition leader Machado returns from exile, received by thousands of supporters in Caracas
clusters.summary: Nobel Peach Prize winner and popular Venezuelan political opposition figure Maria Corina Machado has returned from nearly a year in exile. She was greeted by thousands of cheering supporters in Caracas.

clusters.headline: Indonesia says gas export cuts to Singapore within contractual limits, pledges to honour obligations
clusters.summary: The cuts fall within the minimum contractual limits of around 91 to 92 per cent of exports, says Coordinating Minister for Downstreaming and Energy Transition Bahlil Lahadalia.

clusters.headline: Kenya: Police Rescue 59 Ethiopians, Including Four-Year-Old Child, in Marsabit Smuggling Operation
clusters.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Police have rescued 59 Ethiopian nationals, including a four-year-old child, in a multi-agency operation targeting suspected human smuggling in Marsabit County.

clusters.headline: Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
clusters.summary: The populist right-wing leader of 12 years says it is "clear" his party has lost the vote billed as a referendum on the country's future.
